newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba sees German prices as stable in near term.
newsitem.headline: Buba sees German prices as stable in near term.

text.p: German prices look set to remain stable in the near future, the Bundesbank said in its September report released on Thursday.

"Consumer prices do not show signs of endangering price stability in the near-term," the Bundesbank wrote, reemphasising a widely-held view that even as economic growth revives, inflationary pressures are still under control.

The Bundesbank said the calm price climate was one of several factors paving the way to last month's easing, when the central bank sliced a hefty 30 basis points off its main money market rate, the repo, moving it to three percent.
Similarly, news that M3 money supply growth, a key policy guideline as it foreshadows future inflation rates, has been slowing consistently, had allowed the policy move.

Finally, the Bundesbank said, "the interest rate reduction fit into the international environment," noting in particular that the mark had appreciated over the summer months, effectively tightening domestic monetary conditions.
But despite the current moderate price climate, the central bank sought to reemphasise that its most recent decision should not lead markets to expect more steps immediately.
"With its clear reduction of the repo rate, the Bundesbank has created clarity in monetary policy for the time being," the central bank said.

The central bank also sought to underscore its independence by saying, "with this monetary policy, not dictated by short-term market expectations but rather oriented towards price stability, we created conditions that should foster long-term investment decisions as well as steady and appropriate economic growth."
The Bundesbank said that its policies would not create inflationary pressures stemming from the monetary side.
Meanwhile the outlook for money supply developments were "not bad, even though it may be difficult to bring M3 back into the (four to seven percent) target corridor by the end of the year."
